## Label quality signals (no label was changed)

* 37 reviews rated 1–2 stars carry the human label *positive*; 3 reviews rated 4–5 stars carry *negative*.
* 58 reviews labelled *positive* by a human were predicted *negative* by few-shot; 33 of them are rated 1–2 stars.
* Several of these read as clearly negative (e.g. a 2-star review that only says coffee grounds end up in the coffee). The scores above therefore partly measure label noise. A review of these labels by the annotators is recommended before the result is treated as final; any change must be made by a human on the Human Annotation page and the evaluation rerun (`python scripts/d2_human_eval.py evaluate`).

## Relation to the historical (mostly AI-assisted) reference labels

The human label equals the historical reference label for 147 of 300 reviews (0.4900). Historical distribution: {'positive': 111, 'negative': 141, 'neutral': 6, 'mixed': 42}; human distribution: {'positive': 166, 'negative': 43, 'neutral': 55, 'mixed': 36}. Because the reference changed this much, the scores above are not comparable with the historical 299-review evaluation (macro F1 0.4380 / 0.6025 / 0.4232), which is kept unchanged in the run's metrics.json.

## Limitations

* One label per review by one of four annotators; no second-person verification and no inter-annotator agreement was measured.
* Annotators labelled different subsets of different sizes (100/83/62/55); the allocation was not balanced.
* Stored predictions were re-scored; the predictions for the supplementary review were produced later (2026-11-14) with the same model, prompt version and settings.
* Sentiment and star rating disagree for some reviews (e.g. positive labels on 1–2-star reviews); labels were not changed.
